title: Grammar: Linking Words — Cause, Effect, Sequence, and Summary
grammarTip:
Маркеры причины и следствия в академическом письме:

ПРИЧИНА → СЛЕДСТВИЕ:
because / since / as → простая причина
due to / owing to / as a result of + noun → формально
"Due to the increase in temperature, the glacier is melting."

СЛЕДСТВИЕ → ПРИЧИНА:
therefore / consequently / as a result / hence / thus
"Temperatures have risen. Consequently, glaciers are retreating."
"The deadline was missed; therefore, the project was delayed."

💡 Позиция маркера:
Начало предложения: "Therefore, the results were inconclusive."
Середина: "The results, therefore, were inconclusive."
После точки с запятой: "...; therefore, ..."

Точка зрения vs факт: "hence" и "thus" → более формальны чем "so"

grammarTable.subject: CAUSE
grammarTable.verb: because, since, as, owing to, due to, as a result of, on account of
grammarTable.example: "The film succeeded owing to its unconventional structure and strong performances."

grammarTable.subject: EFFECT
grammarTable.verb: therefore, consequently, as a result, thus, hence, for this reason
grammarTable.example: "The director trusted the audience; consequently, the film avoids over-explanation."

grammarTable.subject: PURPOSE
grammarTable.verb: in order to, so as to, so that, with the aim of
grammarTable.example: "The director uses silence in order to create discomfort in the viewer."

grammarTable.subject: SEQUENCE
grammarTable.verb: firstly, secondly, then, subsequently, finally, in conclusion
grammarTable.example: "Firstly, consider the structure. Then, examine the language choices."

grammarTable.subject: SUMMARY
grammarTable.verb: in conclusion, to sum up, overall, in short, on balance
grammarTable.example: "On balance, despite its flaws, the film is a significant achievement."

grammarTable.subject: CONDITION
grammarTable.verb: if, provided that, as long as, on condition that, unless
grammarTable.example: "A film succeeds provided that it achieves what it set out to do."

rows.form: because / since / as + clause
rows.example: "The film resonates because it depicts universal human experience."

rows.form: owing to / due to / as a result of + noun or gerund
rows.example: "Owing to its ambiguous ending, the film has divided critics."

rows.form: "Due to" vs "owing to": both correct, "due to" slightly more formal in written form
rows.example: "Due to budget constraints, the film relied on natural lighting." ✅

rows.form: "On account of" = formal, same as "owing to"
rows.example: "On account of its literary quality, the novel won the Booker Prize."

grammarExtra.title: Effect Linkers: Showing Consequence in Analysis

rows.form: Therefore / Thus: formal, logical consequence
rows.example: "The director rejects conventional plotting; therefore, the audience must construct meaning actively."

rows.form: Consequently: strong formal effect marker
rows.example: "The film's ambiguity is carefully constructed; consequently, no reading fully satisfies."

rows.form: As a result: neutral and clear
rows.example: "The novel was banned in several countries. As a result, its readership grew."

rows.form: Hence: very formal, often academic
rows.example: "The imagery is deliberately ambiguous; hence the multiple critical interpretations."

rows.form: in order to + infinitive
rows.example: "She uses fragmented time in order to disorient the viewer and reflect the character's mental state."

rows.form: so as to + infinitive (often negative)
rows.example: "The director keeps the camera distant so as not to impose an emotional interpretation."

rows.form: so that + clause
rows.example: "The author withholds information so that the reader experiences the character's confusion directly."

rows.form: with the aim of + gerund (formal)
rows.example: "The artist uses colour symbolically with the aim of reinforcing the film's themes."

rows.form: Firstly / First of all… Secondly… Finally
rows.example: "Firstly, I will examine the structure. Secondly, I will analyse the language. Finally, I will evaluate the overall impact."

rows.form: Then / Subsequently / Following this
rows.example: "The director establishes the setting. Then, she introduces the central conflict."

rows.form: In the first place / In the second place (formal)
rows.example: "In the first place, the narrative structure is unusual."

rows.form: Last but not least / Most importantly
rows.example: "Last but not least, the film's use of silence deserves attention."

rows.form: In conclusion / To conclude: formal final paragraph opener
rows.example: "In conclusion, despite its flaws, the film represents a genuine artistic achievement."

rows.form: On balance: acknowledging both sides before final judgement
rows.example: "On balance, the novel's strengths significantly outweigh its weaknesses."

rows.form: Overall / In short / To sum up: neutral summary
rows.example: "Overall, this is a film that demands — and rewards — careful attention."

rows.form: Ultimately: the final, deepest conclusion
rows.example: "Ultimately, the film succeeds because it trusts its audience."

exercises.text: "The film was banned in several countries ___ its explicit political content."

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct effect linker.
exercises.text: "The novel's ending is deeply ambiguous. ___, readers have interpreted it in contradictory ways." (result)
exercises.hint: "As a result / Consequently" = showing the effect of what came before

exercises.text: "The director uses extreme close-ups ___ create a sense of claustrophobia."
exercises.hint: "In order to + infinitive" = explaining artistic intention

exercises.text: "___, I will examine the film's structure. ___, I will analyse the cinematography. ___, I will evaluate its overall impact."

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct cause linker + structure.
exercises.text: "___ the film's commercial failure, it went on to win critical acclaim."
exercises.hint: "Despite + noun" = concession — but this is concession, not cause. Use "Despite" for contrast with expectation.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct conclusion linker.
exercises.text: "___, this novel represents a major achievement in contemporary fiction — ambitious, moving, and formally daring." (summarising)
exercises.hint: Summary linker at the start of a concluding statement

exercises.text: "The author withholds the protagonist's name ___ emphasise their lack of identity."
exercises.hint: "So as to + infinitive" = purpose (often emphasising the reason)

exercises.instruction: Choose the most formal effect linker.
exercises.text: "The film's score was unanimously praised; ___, the director chose the same composer for her next project."
exercises.hint: "Hence" = very formal effect marker, used in written academic analysis

exercises.text: "___ its unusual narrative structure, the novel was initially rejected by several publishers."
exercises.correct: Due to / Owing to / Because of

exercises.instruction: Which is the best concluding sentence for a film review?
opts: The film is therefore very good.
On balance, despite its structural weaknesses, the film succeeds as an emotionally resonant and visually extraordinary experience.
To sum up: I liked it.
In conclusion, the film was fine.
exercises.correct: On balance, despite its structural weaknesses, the film succeeds as an emotionally resonant and visually extraordinary experience.
exercises.hint: "On balance" + concession + strong evaluative statement = strong conclusion

exercises.text: "The writer uses fragmented dialogue ___ the reader feels the disconnection between the characters."
exercises.hint: "So that + subject + verb" = purpose (the goal or intended effect)

exercises.instruction: Which shows the effect of an artistic choice most precisely?
exercises.text: "The director uses a handheld camera. ___ the viewer feels physically present in the scene."
exercises.hint: "As a result" = the direct consequence of the artistic choice

exercises.text: "The director ___ establishes the setting. ___ this, she introduces the main conflict." (what comes after)

exercises.instruction: Which summary linker best introduces a balanced final judgment?
exercises.hint: "On balance" = weighing both sides and reaching a final judgment

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct formal cause linker.
exercises.text: "___ its commercial failure, the film was never widely distributed." (= because of)", formal)
exercises.correct: Owing to / Due to / On account of
exercises.hint: "Owing to / Due to / On account of + noun" = formal cause

exercises.instruction: Which is the most sophisticated way to express artistic purpose?
exercises.text: "The director uses slow motion to make the audience think about time."
opts: The director uses slow motion so we think about time.
The director uses slow motion in order to prompt the audience to reflect on the nature of time.
The director uses slow motion because time.
The director uses slow motion and so people think.
exercises.correct: The director uses slow motion in order to prompt the audience to reflect on the nature of time.
exercises.hint: "In order to + infinitive" = formal artistic intention; precise vocabulary

questions.text: "___ its unconventional structure, the film was commercially successful." (cause: explains the success)
"The novel's language is dense and complex. ___, first-time readers often find it challenging." (effect)
"The director keeps the camera at a distance ___ avoid imposing an emotional response on the viewer."
"___, the film examines identity. Secondly, it explores memory. Finally, it questions narrative itself."
"___, despite occasional weaknesses, this film represents a significant artistic achievement." (conclusion)
questions.hint: Summary linker for a concluding paragraph

questions.text: "The film used natural light. Hence, the result felt realistic." — This is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: "Hence" = formal effect marker (very formal, used in academic writing)

questions.text: "The author withholds information ___ the reader experiences the narrator's confusion directly." (purpose — reader is the subject of the clause)
questions.hint: "So that + subject + verb" = purpose with a new subject

questions.text: "___ the film's slow pacing, it failed to attract mainstream audiences."
questions.hint: "Owing to + noun" = the cause of what followed

questions.text: "___ ___, both the structure and the language contribute to the novel's power. ___." (sequence + summary)
"The score was criticised, ___ the cast's performances were universally praised." (contrast within one sentence)
"___ its difficult subject matter, the film found a surprisingly large audience." (unexpected positive despite negative condition)
"___, the film succeeds on its own terms, though it will not appeal to all audiences." (balanced final conclusion)
questions.hint: "On balance" = weighing all considerations before a final judgement
